title: CanonFedRec: A Canonical Geometric Framework for Personalized Federated Recommendation

problem.claim: Federated recommendation frameworks struggle to preserve universal aggregated item representations while handling heterogeneous client data, causing memory costs and reduced recommendation diversity.

gap.claim: The failure of aggregated item embeddings is attributed to server-side Global Geometric Misalignment and client-side Local Filtering Bubbles.

contributions.claim: CanonFedRec addresses the identified federated recommendation challenges through a canonical geometric perspective.
The framework shifts optimization from Euclidean space to a unit hypersphere and uses Riemannian Projection-based Aggregation for geometrically compatible global updates.
The framework uses Divergence-Aware Elastic Alignment to treat item-wise variance as a proxy for client cognitive divergence and dynamically adapt optimization objectives.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe CanonFedRec as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four datasets reportedly show improved representational power of aggregated item embeddings and superior performance.
The framework reportedly reduces memory costs by up to 40× compared with the best FedRec approach.

narrative_sequence.summary: Privacy demands have made federated recommendation an important research topic.
Existing approaches decouple item representations, weakening aggregation universality and collaborative benefits while increasing memory costs and reducing diversity.
The authors identify global geometric misalignment and local filtering bubbles as causes of aggregated item-embedding failure.
CanonFedRec applies hyperspherical optimization, Riemannian projection-based aggregation, and divergence-aware elastic alignment.
Experiments on four datasets report stronger representations, better performance, and up to 40× lower memory costs.

source_observation.claim: The proposed framework separates magnitude noise from semantic relationships by optimizing item representations on a unit hypersphere.

interpretation.claim: Geometric normalization may help isolate task-relevant relational structure from nuisance variation.

application.claim: For distributed representation learning with heterogeneous client scales, consider geometry-aware normalization before aggregation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond federated recommendation or across other representation geometries.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not provide theoretical results, proof details, or implementation and reproducibility information.
